title: Weekly arXiv physics — 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-06 UTC: 7 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending or readership chart; ordering is inferred from checkable attention and research signals. Citation evidence is limited for papers only days old, and Semantic Scholar citation fields could not be retrieved for this snapshot.

sections.title: Observation of light-induced Haldane gap in graphene
sections.abstract: The authors report a transient Dirac gap in monolayer graphene that appears only under circularly polarized driving, identifying it with a light-induced Haldane mass and Floquet topology.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a 203 ± 30 meV light-induced Dirac gap under circularly polarized mid-infrared pumping, absent under linear polarization; time-resolved spectra and Floquet calculations link it to dynamical time-reversal-symmetry breaking.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on monolayer graphene, interpreted with Floquet calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The effect is transient and measured in a particular pump–probe regime on monolayer graphene; the topological Berry-curvature/Chern interpretation is supported by calculations rather than a transport measurement of a quantized response.

sections.title: Probing the charm-quark dead cone effect in heavy ion collisions
sections.abstract: The CMS authors measure late, collinear jet emissions in PbPb collisions and find a suppression of small-angle emissions in prompt-D⁰-tagged jets consistent with the charm-quark dead-cone effect.
sections.claimed_result: CMS reports that D⁰-tagged jets have fewer small-angle splittings than inclusive jets in PbPb data, consistent with the charm dead cone; its PbPb-to-pp comparison disfavors scenarios with strong filling of that cone by medium-induced radiation.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 2018 CMS PbPb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV, with 1.7 nb⁻¹ integrated luminosity and late-kT jet grooming.
sections.unique_caveat: Within the measured kinematic range and precision, the PbPb-versus-pp comparison shows no significant difference and has limited power to distinguish the jet-medium models considered by the authors.

sections.title: A search for sterile neutrinos at ultrahigh energies at the Pierre Auger Observatory
sections.abstract: The Pierre Auger authors model Earth-skimming and upward-going air showers to set limits on ultrahigh-energy fluxes of MeV–100 MeV sterile neutrinos mixing mainly with tau neutrinos, and derive benchmark constraints for superheavy dark matter decays.
sections.claimed_result: For an E⁻² spectrum and sin²θN ≲ 10⁻¹, the authors derive a 90% confidence upper limit of approximately E²ΦN ≤ 2 × 10⁻⁹ sin⁻²θN GeV cm⁻² sr⁻¹ s⁻¹ over 0.3–200 EeV; the paper also gives benchmark dark-matter-decay constraints.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; Monte Carlo exposure calculation for the Pierre Auger Observatory using observed air-shower event samples.
sections.unique_caveat: The limits are sensitivity constraints, not evidence of a signal; the authors' benchmark sterile-neutrino fluxes lie several orders below current sensitivity, and tau-lepton energy-loss modeling contributes a dominant +34%/−28% exposure uncertainty.

sections.title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
sections.abstract: The DESI authors combine four mock-calibrated dynamical methods applied to DR2 halo-star data to estimate the Milky Way's mass and quantify method-dependent biases and correlations.
sections.claimed_result: From 10,036 RR Lyrae and blue-horizontal-branch stars, the authors report a joint mass within 80 kpc of 6.36⁺⁰·⁵³₋₀·⁴⁸ × 10¹¹ M☉ and a virial M200c of 1.19⁺⁰·¹⁴₋₀·¹² × 10¹² M☉ after mock-based corrections.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; DESI DR2 six-dimensional halo-star data, calibrated against cosmological mock surveys and Gaia DR3-like uncertainties.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimates depend on mock calibration, selection-function assumptions, and residual correlations among methods; the authors note that method-specific results can differ despite the joint estimate.

sections.title: A multiprobe ΛCDM consistency analysis with gravitational-wave standard sirens
sections.abstract: The authors combine LVK GWTC-5.0 standard sirens with DES, DESI, supernova, and CMB measurements to assess ΛCDM consistency and the H₀ and S₈ tensions.
sections.claimed_result: Adding standard sirens improves the Ωm–S₈ constraints by about 30% and yields a 6.2% H₀ constraint in the authors' analysis, while neither the S₈ discrepancy nor the H₀ tension is materially reduced at current GW sensitivity.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; LVK GWTC-5.0, DES Year 6 lensing and clustering, DESI BAO, Type Ia supernovae, and Planck/ACT/SPT CMB data combined with normalizing flows.
sections.unique_caveat: The present standard-siren precision is not enough to resolve either tension; the inferred constraints remain conditional on the adopted joint-probe analysis and its common priors.

sections.title: Latest νs from the Earliest Galaxies: Probing neutrino self-interactions with JWST
sections.abstract: The authors use high-redshift JWST ultraviolet luminosity-function data together with Planck CMB data to constrain beyond-Standard-Model neutrino self-interactions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 95% upper limits on log₁₀(Geff/MeV⁻²) of about −2.75 for one interacting neutrino flavor and ≲−3.41 when all three flavors interact, stronger than their Planck-only constraints.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; cosmological inference combining Planck CMB and JWST high-redshift UV luminosity-function measurements.
sections.unique_caveat: These are model-dependent parameter constraints, not a detection of neutrino self-interactions; they depend on the assumed neutrino-interaction scenario and interpretation of the high-redshift galaxy luminosity function.

sections.title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
sections.abstract: The authors use IceCube's measured neutrino flavor composition to constrain tau–sterile mixing and project the reach of future neutrino telescopes.
sections.claimed_result: Fitting IceCube flavor-composition data while leaving the source composition free, the authors obtain |Uτ4|² < 0.88 at 90% confidence; their projected combined sensitivity reaches 0.24–0.29 by 2040 and 0.12–0.14 by 2050 under the stated future-instrument assumptions.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; inference from IceCube flavor-composition measurements, followed by future-sensitivity forecasts.
sections.unique_caveat: The present bound is weak, and projected improvement depends on future detector performance and flavor-composition assumptions; these forecasts are not future measurements.
